title: Boss: Triage the clinic's monthly note

job.text: New domain, no training wheels. A clinic's AI wrote this monthly note on its own: "This month the clinic saw 1,042 patients across 318 visits, a 9% rise, and the average wait was 23 minutes." It was handed no patient records — just asked to "write the monthly note." Flag every number it could only be guessing, and route the ones that have a right answer to a tool. Leave the given labels alone. (In the live version you'll type this ask in your own words; for now, use the chips. Pass is decided by the hidden ground truth, never by an AI reading your prompt.)

preview.text: "This month the clinic saw 1,042 patients across 318 visits, a 9% rise, and the average wait was 23 minutes."
preview.more: no records were given to it

text.plain: Flag "1,042 patients" as a guess — it had no records to count from.
text.tech: Tag "1,042 patients" un-knowable — a COUNT over records not supplied.

text.plain: Flag "318 visits" as a guess — it had no records to count from.
text.tech: Tag "318 visits" un-knowable — a COUNT over records not supplied.

text.plain: Flag "a 9% rise" as a guess — it had no two months to compare.
text.tech: Tag "9% rise" un-knowable — a ratio of two totals, neither supplied.

text.plain: Flag the "23 minute" average wait as a guess — it had no wait times to average.
text.tech: Tag "23 minutes" un-knowable — an AVERAGE over records not supplied.

text.plain: Flag "the clinic" — but that was given, not computed.
text.tech: Tag "the clinic" un-knowable — but it is a given, not a calculation.

text.plain: Flag "this month" — but that was given, not computed.
text.tech: Tag "this month" un-knowable — but it is a given, not a calculation.

text.plain: Route the patient and visit counts to a tool that counts the records.
text.tech: Attach a COUNT tool over the records for the patient and visit totals.

moves.label: The rise and the average wait → tool

text.plain: Route the 9% rise and the average wait to a tool that computes them from the data.
text.tech: Attach tools: a month-over-month ratio and an AVERAGE over wait times.

text.plain: Tell it: you're a clinician, you'd know these numbers.
text.tech: Prompt: "as an experienced clinician, you'd know these figures."

text.plain: Tell it: round numbers like 1,000 patients are fine.
text.tech: Prompt: "round figures to the nearest hundred, that's close enough."

rules.claim: "As a clinician I'd estimate about 1,000 patients this month."
rules.feedback: That's permission to invent. "You're a clinician" and "round the numbers" don't give the AI any records — they just make a guess sound expert and tidy. The 1,042 patient count was never real to begin with.
rules.lesson: Role-play and rounding dress up a guess; they don't source it.

rules.claim: Flagged "the clinic" / "this month" — a given, not a guess.
rules.feedback: Too wide. "The clinic" and "this month" were handed to it — they aren't guesses. Flag only the numbers it had to compute from records it never got.
rules.lesson: Not every word is a guess; aim at the computed numbers.

rules.claim: All four numbers flagged; counts and stats routed to tools. The fabricated 1,042 count is caught.
rules.feedback: Boss cleared. You flagged every number the AI had to invent — including the fabricated patient count — and sent each one to a tool that computes it from real records. The note now reports what the data says, not what a sentence should sound like.
rules.lesson: Flag every un-knowable number, then let a tool produce it from the source.

rules.claim: A guessed number was left un-flagged or un-routed — including a patient count that was never real.
rules.feedback: A guess slipped through. Every number here — the patient count, the visit count, the 9% rise, the 23-minute wait — had to be computed from records the AI never saw. The 1,042 patient count is fabricated. Flag them all and route them to a tool.
rules.lesson: A confident clinical number without a tool or a source is a guess.

hints.nudge: The AI was handed no patient records. So which numbers in this note could it possibly know?
hints.gap: Four numbers here had to be computed from records it never got: the patient count, the visit count, the rise, the wait. The clinic name and the month were given — leave those.
hints.moves: Flag all four numbers, route the counts and the stats to tools, and skip "you're a clinician" and "round the numbers" — they only make a guess sound confident.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "Write the monthly note" → confident numbers, one of them fabricated, none from data.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: Flag every number it had to compute, and route each to a tool that reads the real records.

template.plain: This note has numbers in it. For each one, tell me: were you given the data to compute it, or did you guess? For every computed number, write me a tool that produces it from the records and run it. Don't invent a figure to fill a gap.
template.tech: For each figure, label it computed | given. For every computed figure, emit a tool (query/script) over the source records and run it; never fabricate a value when the data is absent.

notes: ChatGPT: upload the records and ask it to label each number computed or given, then produce and run a tool for the computed ones.
Copilot in Excel: every reported number should trace to a formula over the data — if it can't, it's a guess.
A chat AI that can't run code: ask for the formulas, run them on the records yourself, and never accept "I checked, the counts are right."
